widgets_values:
# Mpillow showroom -- one integrated workflow

Read left to right. Five sections:

**1. MOODBOARDS.** One group per area. Each reads two folders in the repo:
`ref-img/moodboard/<area>/` (materials, light, atmosphere) and
`ref-img/furniture/<area>/` (specific pieces). Drop images in, press Run.
The folder loaders hash the files, so only changed areas re-run. The area
prompt in each group drives that moodboard AND the render.

**2. PLAN -> 3D.** The page-4 plan, the dimensioned model
(`tools/build_massing.py` -> `showroom_massing.glb`, shown in Load3D),
and the baked cutaway views (`tools/render_views.py`) that the renders
are locked to. No AI model turns a floor plan into a room; the geometry is
computed from the brief's dimensions.

**3. PROMPTS.** Render base, materials, lighting, then the six area
prompts, concatenated into one final prompt. The preview node shows the
exact text the model receives.

**4. RENDERS.** Six area moodboards -> one master sheet; six furniture
sheets -> one master sheet; then one render per camera view.

**5. CONTROLNET RENDERS.** The same final prompt through Qwen-Image
text-to-image, with the InstantX ControlNet Union pinned to each camera's
depth pass. No reference images go in here: materials and light come from
the prompt, geometry and viewpoint from the depth map. `strength` on each
Apply ControlNet node is the knob (1.0 traces the model exactly). Compare
`renders/final/<view>` (section 4) with `renders/final/<view>_cn`.

Outputs land in the repo: `renders/moodboard/`, `renders/final/`.
Always 16:9 (1664 x 928). Local models only; nothing spends credits.

The Load3D chain is MUTED: its `image` input is a browser viewport
snapshot, so it only works when you press Run in this tab. Un-mute it here
to orbit the model by hand.

---

**ZONED VARIANT.** This copy of the workflow uses the colour ID pass
(`ref-img/massing/massing_<view>_ids.png`) for regional prompting (each
area prompt confined to its own zone mask on top of the whole-scene
prompt, then the depth ControlNet) and produces exactly THREE final
renders in `renders/final/`:

1. `00-sheet_cn_zoned` -- the four isometric cameras in ONE picture
   (5.10). One sampling pass, so materials, furniture and light agree.
   Optional muted 1.5x hi-res refine of the whole sheet (5.10b).
2. `01-section_cn_zoned` -- a section through ONE area, chosen by the
   ZONE number in 5.12 (0 entry .. 5 patio).
3. `02-free-camera_cn_zoned` -- any camera you set by hand in the 3D
   viewer of 5.13 (or by numbers); depth and zone passes are baked live.

Renders 2 and 3 DERIVE from render 1 (5.14): they are drawn beside the
four finished isometric panels in one picture, with only their own two
panels re-noised, so they take the sheet's materials, furniture and
light; then each is cropped and refined at full size.

Section 4 keeps only the master moodboard sheets here.
Built with `python tools/build_workflow.py --zoned`.

widgets_values:
## Floor plan -> 3D

Image-to-3D models (TRELLIS.2, Hunyuan3D, Tripo, Meshy, Rodin) rebuild a
single object from a photo. None of them can read a plan and produce a
room, and the ones installed here are paid cloud APIs.

So the plan on the left is turned into geometry by
`tools/build_massing.py`: every dimension from the brief, every position
read off this drawing. 165 parts, exact to the centimetre.

```
python tools/build_massing.py   # -> model/showroom_massing.glb
python tools/render_views.py    # -> ref-img/massing/*.png
```

Edit a number in the ZONES block, run both, press Run here. The views
below are what the renders are locked to.
nodes.title: 2.2  build_massing.py  (dimensions -> GLB)

widgets_values: A photorealistic architectural interior photograph of a custom pillow showroom, built exactly to the layout shown. Keep every wall, shelf, storage rack, bed, curtain track and workbench in precisely the position, size and proportion given, and keep exactly the same viewpoint. This is a real full-size room with its near walls cut away -- it is NOT a scale model, NOT a dollhouse, NOT a diorama on a table. There is no surrounding room, no floor or rug beneath it and no background object; the interior fills the whole frame. Replace the flat grey surfaces with the real materials, textures and lighting described, as shot on a full-frame camera with a tilt-shift lens, natural film grain, high dynamic range.

widgets_values:
## Section 5 vs section 4

**Section 4** edits the grey massing view with Qwen-Image-Edit, using the
master moodboard and furniture sheets as picture references. It keeps
the geometry but tends to keep the flat CG look too.

**Section 5** generates from scratch with Qwen-Image and pins the result
to the depth pass of the same camera through the InstantX ControlNet
Union. Nothing grey goes in, so the model is free on materials and light;
walls, racks, beds and viewpoint still land where the 3D model puts them.

Knobs:
- `strength` on Apply ControlNet: 1.0 traces the depth exactly, 0.6-0.8
  lets furniture and detail deviate.
- `end_percent` below 1.0 releases the lock for the last steps (finer
  texture, slightly looser geometry).
- `steps` 4 / `cfg` 1.0 go with the Lightning LoRA. Bypass the LoRA and
  use 20 steps / cfg 2.5 for the full-quality model (5x slower).
- `seed` is fixed per view so re-runs are comparable.

Depth maps come from `tools/render_views.py` (near = white). The prompt is
the same final prompt as section 4, so any change in sections 1 or 3
shows in both.
nodes.title: 5  How this differs from section 4

widgets_values:
## Zoned variant

`render_views.py` bakes an **ID pass** per camera: every visible surface
point is painted with the flat colour of the area it sits in (by plan
position). Each colour becomes a mask: R, G and B thresholded at 0.5
and combined with mask arithmetic (red = R - G - B, yellow = R x G - B,
...). An exact-colour match is not used because the image loader and
Render Mesh shift many pixels by a level or two, which left holes. The
area prompt from section 1 is encoded on its own and
`ConditioningSetMask` confines it to that mask. All six sit on top of
the whole-scene prompt
(masked to the full frame at `GLOBAL_STRENGTH`), are combined, and go
through the depth ControlNet and the sampler as in the plain workflow.

The sampler runs the model once per conditioning entry and blends the
results by mask, so a view with six areas costs about 7x the plain
section 5 sampling time (still 4 steps).

Knobs:
- `strength` on the whole-scene mask: lower = area prompts dominate more.
- `strength` on an area mask: raise for a stubborn area, or 0 to drop it.
- colours: red entry, green fitting, blue inventory, yellow workshop,
  magenta service, cyan patio (`render_views.ZONES`).

Three renders come out of this workflow, all through the same zoning:
the SHEET of four isometrics (5.10), one ZONE SECTION you choose by
number (5.12) and one FREE CAMERA you set by hand (5.13). The last two
are drawn beside the finished sheet panels (5.14), so they derive
their materials and light from the isometrics.

## 5.10  The sheet: four isometrics in one picture

Rendering the cameras one at a time draws each from fresh noise, so
materials and furniture drift between them. Here the four depth passes
are tiled 2 x 2 into one control image, the four ID passes into one
mask image, and ONE sampling pass (whole-scene prompt + the six area
prompts confined to their zones on the sheet, depth ControlNet) renders
all four cameras inside one 2048 x 1152 picture. They cannot disagree:
they are decided together in one latent. The sheet is the deliverable;
it is not split up.

**5.10b (optional, muted).** The whole sheet upscaled 1.5x to
3072 x 1728 and refined in place at `denoise` 0.4 with the same masks
and depth lock (ComfyUI resizes both to the latent). Un-mute the Save
node on the right to run it; expect several minutes.

Knobs:
- `seed` on the sheet KSampler: a new seed = a new coherent scheme for
  all four cameras at once.
- `strength` on the sheet's whole-scene mask / area masks: as in 5.9.
- `denoise` on the 5.10b KSampler: 0.3 sharpen only, 0.6 re-imagine.

Outputs: `renders/final/00-sheet_cn_zoned` and, if un-muted,
`renders/final/00-sheet-hires_cn_zoned`.

Tried and dropped: matching each camera to a hero render with
Qwen-Image-Edit-2509. With a photo reference the edit model reproduces
that photo; the depth ControlNet cannot override it.

## 5.12  Zone section: pick one area

`render_views.py` bakes a section per area: the model is clipped to
the area's plan box (cut faces capped) and an orthographic camera looks
in from the open side, 15 degrees from above:

| # | area | looks |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | entry and waiting | west, at the door wall |
| 1 | fitting bays | north, at the beds and photo station |
| 2 | inventory wall | south, at the display wall |
| 3 | workshop | south, bench in front of the inventory wall |
| 4 | service band | east, at the patio glazing |
| 5 | patio | east, at the open side |

All six depth passes and all six ID passes are loaded into two batches;
the **ZONE** number above picks one of each (`Get Image from Batch`).
The chosen ID pass drives the six area masks exactly as on the sheet,
so an area that is not in the picture simply gets an empty mask.

To change the cut, the direction or the pitch, edit `SECTIONS` /
`SEC_PITCH` in `tools/render_views.py`, re-run it, press Run here.

The render itself happens in 5.14, beside the finished isometrics, so
the section takes the sheet's look. Output
`renders/final/01-section_cn_zoned` (ComfyUI numbers the files, so
switching zones does not overwrite the previous one).

## 5.13  Free camera

**HIDE PARTS** (top left) is the layer switch. One glTF part name per
line, `*` `?` wildcards, `#` for a comment: `wall_north`, `poly_roof*`,
`box_??`. The list feeds two `GLB Part Filter` nodes (custom node,
`comfy_nodes/mp_glb_parts`): one drops those parts from the full model,
one drops the same parts from the zone-coloured ID twin, whose pieces
carry a `__z<n>` suffix the match ignores -- so depth and masks always
agree. The default list is the cutaway (north wall + patio roof). Empty
the box for the closed room; switch a filter to `show_only` to keep
just the listed parts. `part names in the model` lists every name you
can type; `hidden now` echoes what matched.

The `Preview 3D (Advanced)` viewer shows the filtered model and IS the
camera: orbit, pan and zoom it by hand, press Run. Its camera goes to
two `Render Mesh` nodes that bake the **depth** pass and the **ID**
pass at 1664 x 928 for that exact camera. Nothing about the camera is
baked in advance, so any angle works, including inside the room; the
camera is saved with the workflow, and the two previews show what the
ControlNet and the zone masks receive.

Prefer numbers? Connect the `Create Camera Info` node to `camera_info`
on BOTH Render Mesh nodes instead (orbit: yaw / pitch / distance around
the target; look_at: an explicit eye position, e.g. 1.6 m high inside).
Render Mesh is always perspective (`fov` from the viewer).

The render itself happens in 5.14, beside the finished isometrics, so
the view takes the sheet's look. Output
`renders/final/02-free-camera_cn_zoned`.

widgets_values:
## 5.14  The section and the free camera derive from the sheet

Drawn on their own, the section and the free camera would start from
fresh noise and pick their own materials. Instead they are drawn NEXT TO
the finished isometrics: the four finished panels are cut out of the
sheet (5.10) at panel size and laid out three by two with two
placeholder panels; the latent of that picture gets a noise mask that
covers only the two placeholders, so the sampler re-draws just those
while attending to the finished panels in the same latent. The depth
sheet and the ID sheet are tiled the same way (iso passes from 5.10,
section passes from 5.12, free camera passes from 5.13), so the two new
panels are depth-locked and zone-prompted exactly like the sheet.

Each new panel is then cropped, upscaled to 1664 x 928 and refined by
its own depth-locked, zone-prompted sampler at `denoise` 0.5: detail
comes back; what the sheet decided stays.

Change the ZONE number (5.12) or move the camera (5.13) and press Run:
5.10 is cached, only this stage and the refine re-run.

Knobs:
- `seed` on the 5.14 KSampler: a new draw of the two panels, same look.
- `denoise` on a refine KSampler: 0.3 sharpen only, 0.6 re-imagine.
- `strength` on the whole-sheet mask: lower = area prompts dominate.

Outputs: `renders/final/01-section_cn_zoned` and
`renders/final/02-free-camera_cn_zoned`.
